result.title: PhysioWave-T: Token-Efficient Wavelet Foundation Models for Biosignals
result.comment: 15 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/ForeverBlue816/PhysioWave , Models & Weights: https://huggingface.co/collections/ForeverBlue/physiowave-t
result.summary: We present PhysioWave-T, a token-efficient wavelet foundation model family for EEG, ECG, and sEMG. Dynamic scale folding recombines J+1 wavelet subbands prior to tokenization, compressing sequence length from (J+1)CS to CS tokens for J levels, C channels, and S temporal patches. Route-specific front ends and learned channel-name embeddings allow one Transformer per modality to handle diverse montages and sampling rates, while unseen setups reuse the backbone via lightweight adapters. We pre-train a 30M-parameter EEG model on over 15M windows (19--128 channels), alongside ECG (30M) and sEMG (12M) encoders. Across four EEG routes, scale folding cuts Transformer latency by 4.0--7.2x and peak memory by 6.8--12.7x over scale expansion without accuracy loss. Our EEG encoder leads 8 of 9 metrics against BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGPT, and surpasses LUNA-L on wearable seizure detection with fewer parameters. Reliability-aware latent fusion (RALF) further integrates summary tokens from independently pre-trained encoders via sample-adaptive weights. On SeizeIT2, RALF raises event sensitivity at 11 false alarms/h from 61.4% to 74.4% and window AUPRC from 0.321 to 0.399 over the best unimodal baseline, outperforming weighted-logit and concatenation fusion across all variants. PhysioWave-T also achieves state-of-the-art sEMG accuracies and top macro-F1 on PTB-XL Super and Chapman-Shaoxing. Code and models: https://github.com/ForeverBlue816/PhysioWave.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PhysioWave-T 生物信号（EEG/ECG/sEMG）小波基础模型族，通过动态尺度折叠在 token 化前合并多级子带压缩序列长度，并用可靠性感知的 latent 融合（RALF）以样本自适应权重整合多个独立预训练编码器的摘要 token。
AI.relevance_reason: RALF 的样本自适应、按可靠性加权融合多个摘要表示，可能可供核查 LVR 中多种 latent 假设或视觉证据与推理状态的融合与筛选；尺度折叠带来的 token 长度—延迟/内存权衡也可对照 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本分析，但论文为生理信号模态，迁移性未经视觉推理验证。
